rationale: B wins because it forces the founder to prove the dangerous parts before pitching them: "Without the investigator on record, this angle collapses" is the line a grown-up strategist writes. A is solid, but "Beds are becoming health sensors, one mattress cover at a time" sells a category trend from one company launch, then quietly asks for external examples after the fact. B has one too-clever overreach, but its study-process angle and proof gates are more useful before anyone wastes a reporter's time.
gaps_in_A: "live clinical study with an unnamed sleep clinic" contradicts the update, which says the clinic is named. Small factual wobble, big trust problem.
"Beds are becoming health sensors, one mattress cover at a time" overstates the trend from a single launch; the set admits "there's no broader supplied signal beyond it."
"For athletes chasing recovery data" is plausible, but it rests on marketing audience alone. Without a named athlete or biohacker user, it is still mostly a product-vertical angle.

The category angle claims a "closed loop" around sensing and temperature, but the update does not say the temperature changes are specifically triggered by low SpO2 or snoring. A catches this later, but the headline body gets ahead of the facts.
gaps_in_B: "Snoring detection lands in the biohacker bed before it lands in the sleep clinic" is too cute and too loose. Sleep clinics already deal with snoring/oxygen signals, and the update says a sleep-clinic study is already ongoing.
"the sensors ship in the hardware" is not established. The update says the features are software-gated, not that every non-subscriber owns dormant sensors.
"a privately held company funding or partnering on research" smuggles in a funding concern before the facts support it. Asking who funds the study is right; implying funding happened is not.

"CPAP makers and home sleep-test vendors own the snoring-and-oxygen territory" imports market context not provided in the update. It may be true, but this exercise asked for grounded angles, not confident seasoning.
